Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to consolidate the outstanding privacy items before we proceed to SOW sign-off. Two high‑priority asks from legal & product: a hard no-training/no-model-improvement commitment for pilot data, and clear ownership/entitlement for prompts and generated responses (we need to retain exportability for audit).

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will commit (contractually) that pilot data will not be used to improve or retrain any model variant (no-adaptive training), including any downstream subprocessor activity?
- Where prompt & response logs will be stored, retention defaults, and whether Acme can get an export (SFTP or API) of the session transcripts if requested?
- If there are any subprocessors that will see raw interactions during the pilot and whether geo-routing (US-only) is enforceable for this account.

Attached the SOW v2 for context. We are targeting a Nov 15 start; procurement would like DPA redlines and operational evidence by next week to keep that timeline.

Appreciate a consolidated mutual action plan (MAP) and any operational proofs (subprocessor list, escape hatch for KMS, evidence of per-tenant isolation).

Best,
Emma

Sr. Product Manager, Acme Health

Emma — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front, then a proposed MAP with owners & dates.

Short answers:
- Contractual no-training: Yes — Redwood can commit to a documented no-adaptive-training clause scoped to the pilot interactions. We will include an explicit prohibition on using pilot data for model training or evaluation, and extend the restriction to subprocessors in scope.
- Prompt/response custody & export: We store interaction logs in a per-tenant bucket (encrypted). We can provide an SFTP export or API dump. Retention is configurable; default pilot retention is 30 days, can be set to customer requested period.
- Subprocessors & geo-routing: We will provide a current subprocessor inventory and can enforce region-restricted routing to US-only hosts for this account, subject to contractual SLA on availability.

Proposed MAP (minimal):
1) Legal redline sent to Acme by Redwood counsel — lauren_bishop — by 2026-11-03 (Deliverable: DPA with no-train clause + ownership language).
2) Ops evidence pack — ben_carter/david_kim — by 2026-11-04 (Deliverable: subprocessor list, architecture diagram showing per-tenant isolation, KMS residency statement).
3) Technical confirmation & export test — karthik_iyer / eng — by 2026-11-06 (Deliverable: test SFTP export of 100 sample transcripts).
4) Exec sign-off & DocuSign — mutual — target 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-12.

Lauren & Ben: any additions or must-have language you want me to flag to Acme before Lauren sends redline?

Thanks — Karthik

Emma / team — looping in legal. Attaching a redline draft (sent as DocuSign link) and excerpted clause language below for quick review. I tried to keep it procurement-friendly while preserving operational guardrails.

Key contractual bullets I recommend we provide in the DPA addendum:
- No-Model-Improvement Commitment: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, transcripts, or derived outputs) to train, fine-tune or improve any models, nor permit its subprocessors to do so, for the duration of the Pilot and for [90] days thereafter, except with Customer's prior written consent."
- Prompt/Response Ownership & Exportability: "Customer retains all rights in Customer Data. Upon request, Redwood will provide export of interaction logs in machine-readable JSON or CSV via SFTP/API within 5 business days."
- Subprocessor Access & Evidence: Redwood will provide a current subprocessor list and a written attestation that no subprocessor will use Customer Data for model improvement.
- Geo-routing & KMS: Guarantee routing to US-only infrastructure for the account and the option to use Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for tenant encryption; HSM-level escrow options follow enterprise plan.
- Audit & Proofs: Operational evidence pack (subprocessor inventory, network zoning diagram, retention config) to be delivered prior to execution.

I will send a formal redline link by EOD to Emma and procurement. One ask for Acme: confirm the retention window you require for the pilot exports and whether SFTP or API is preferred.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Emma — quick operational notes. We will prepare the evidence pack and include:

- A per-tenant architecture sketch showing isolation & encryption boundary.
- KMS statement: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and can enable BYOK for pilot.
